mcqs.question: In the Harish Rana case, which condition had the patient remained in for more than 13 years after sustaining injuries in a fall in 2013?
options: Persistent Vegetative State
Coma caused by active euthanasia
Permanent legal incapacity
Brain death following withdrawal of treatment
mcqs.explanation: Harish Rana had been in a Persistent Vegetative State for more than 13 years after the 2013 fall. The case did not describe brain death or active euthanasia.

mcqs.question: In the Harish Rana case, how did the Supreme Court characterise Clinically Assisted Nutrition and Hydration (CANH)?
options: As medical treatment that could be withdrawn in the patient's best interest
As a form of active euthanasia that had to be administered indefinitely
As a judicial punishment imposed on the hospital
As a living will prepared by the family
mcqs.explanation: The Supreme Court held that CANH is medical treatment and that it may be withdrawn in the patient's best interest with the involvement of the family and medical boards. It was not treated as active euthanasia or as a living will.

mcqs.question: What was the holding of Gian Kaur v. State of Punjab (1996) in relation to the right to die?
options: It recognised a right to die under Article 21
It rejected the right to die while recognising the right to live with dignity
It permitted passive euthanasia in exceptional cases
It introduced simplified living wills
mcqs.explanation: Gian Kaur recognised the right to live with dignity but rejected a right to die. Permission for passive euthanasia in exceptional cases came in Aruna Shanbaug, not Gian Kaur.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): P. Rathinam (1994) was overruled by Gian Kaur (1996).
Reason (R): P. Rathinam had recognised a right to die under Article 21, whereas Gian Kaur rejected the right to die.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, and the contrast between the two holdings explains why P. Rathinam was overruled. P. Rathinam recognised a right to die, while Gian Kaur rejected it.

mcqs.question: Which Supreme Court case held that passive euthanasia could be permitted in exceptional cases?
options: Gian Kaur v. State of Punjab
Aruna Shanbaug v. Union of India
Common Cause v. Union of India
P. Rathinam
mcqs.explanation: Aruna Shanbaug v. Union of India (2011) held that passive euthanasia could be allowed in exceptional cases. Gian Kaur rejected a right to die, while Common Cause dealt with refusal of treatment and living wills.

mcqs.keyword: Living wills and refusal of treatment
mcqs.question: Which case recognised the right to refuse treatment and dealt with living wills, whose guidelines were simplified in 2023?
options: Common Cause v. Union of India
Aruna Shanbaug v. Union of India
Hussainara Khatoon
P. Rathinam
mcqs.explanation: Common Cause v. Union of India (2018) recognised the right to refuse treatment and addressed living wills; the guidelines were simplified in 2023. Aruna Shanbaug concerned passive euthanasia in exceptional cases.

mcqs.question: Which pairing correctly reflects the Article 21 cases associated with the subjects mentioned in the Harish Rana legal context?
options: Hussainara Khatoon—speedy trial; Suchita Srivastava and Puttaswamy—reproductive choice
Hussainara Khatoon—living wills; Suchita Srivastava and Puttaswamy—industrial disputes
Hussainara Khatoon—reproductive choice; Suchita Srivastava and Puttaswamy—speedy trial
Hussainara Khatoon—passive euthanasia; Suchita Srivastava and Puttaswamy—sovereign functions
mcqs.explanation: Hussainara Khatoon is associated with speedy trial, while Suchita Srivastava and Puttaswamy are associated with reproductive choice. The other pairings attach unrelated subjects to these cases.

mcqs.question: The nine-judge Constitution Bench hearing the meaning of “industry” is re-examining which 1978 judgment?
options: Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board v. A. Rajappa
State of UP v. Jai Bir Singh
Gian Kaur v. State of Punjab
Common Cause v. Union of India
mcqs.explanation: The case under re-examination is Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board v. A. Rajappa (1978). State of UP v. Jai Bir Singh is a later reference concerning the development of the issue.

mcqs.keyword: Scope and amendment of industry law
mcqs.question:
With reference to the legal developments following the 1978 industry judgment, consider the following statements:
1. The judgment brought hospitals, universities, charities and some welfare departments under labour law.
2. The Industrial Disputes (Amendment) Act, 1982, which sought to exclude hospitals, education and sovereign functions, was notified and implemented.
3. The 1982 amendment sought to exclude hospitals, education and sovereign functions.
options: 1 and 2 only
2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the judgment brought several service and welfare institutions under labour law, and the 1982 amendment sought to exclude specified areas. Statement 2 is incorrect because the amendment was never notified.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the differing decisions concerning Forest Departments in Maharashtra and Gujarat?
options: In 1996 the Maharashtra Forest Department was held to be an industry, while in 2001 the Gujarat Forest Department received the opposite ruling.
In 2001 the Maharashtra Forest Department was held to be an industry, while in 1996 the Gujarat Forest Department received the opposite ruling.
Both the Maharashtra and Gujarat Forest Departments were held to be industries in 1996.
Both the Maharashtra and Gujarat Forest Departments were held not to be industries in 2001.
mcqs.explanation: The Maharashtra Forest Department was held to be an industry in 1996, whereas the Gujarat Forest Department received the opposite treatment in 2001. The years and States are reversed in the tempting alternatives.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: State of UP v. Jai Bir Singh was a five-judge reference in 2001.
Statement B: In 2017, a five-judge bench referred the matter to a seven-judge bench.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are false. State of UP v. Jai Bir Singh was a five-judge reference in 2005, and in 2017 a seven-judge bench referred the matter to a nine-judge bench.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are correct with reference to the proceedings on the meaning of “industry”?
1. The issues include the validity of the triple test in light of the 1982 amendment and the Industrial Relations Code, 2020.
2. The meaning of sovereign functions is one of the issues framed.
3. The 1978 judgment paragraphs under review are 140 and 144.
4. A Constitution Bench under Article 145(3) must have at least three judges.
options: Only one
Only two
Only three
All four
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: the validity of the triple test, sovereign functions, and paragraphs 140 and 144 are among the identified matters. Statement 4 is incorrect because Article 145(3) requires at least five judges.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II in relation to transgender rights and the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, 2026.

List-I
 a. NALSA v. Union of India (2014)
 b. Transgender Persons Act, 2019
 c. Union Minister associated with the Bill
 d. Post-recognition documentary change

List-II
 i. Virendra Kumar
 ii. Gender can be changed in documents, including birth certificates
 iii. Third gender and self-determination of gender identity
 iv. Self-identification, DM certification and National Council
options: a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii
a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i
a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii
a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-iii, b-iv, c-i and d-ii. NALSA recognised third gender and self-determination, the 2019 Act provided the stated framework, Virendra Kumar was associated with the Bill, and recognition permits changes in documents including birth certificates.

mcqs.question:
With reference to transgender persons in India, consider the following statements:
1. Census 2011 recorded approximately 4.88 lakh transgender persons, with the highest numbers in Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra.
2. The World Bank estimated that inclusion could add 1.7% to GDP.
3. The Koovagam Festival is a statutory body created under the 2019 Act.
options: 1 and 2 only
2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Census 2011 recorded approximately 4.88 lakh transgender persons and the World Bank linked inclusion with a possible 1.7% GDP gain. Statement 3 is incorrect because Koovagam Festival is listed as a relevant cultural fact, not as a statutory body under the 2019 Act.

mcqs.question: What income threshold is specified for transgender persons to receive free legal aid from Legal Services Authorities?
options: Below ₹50,000
mcqs.explanation: Legal Services Authorities provide free legal aid to transgender persons with income below ₹2,00,000. The other thresholds do not match the specified eligibility limit.
